title: Casper and the Will
premise: Estate lawyer Lior Galloway is called to read the will of reclusive heiress Vivian Marsh, only to discover the will names Lior personally as executor and witness—despite Lior never having met her. When a body is found in the Marsh estate's conservatory, dressed in clothes stolen from Lior's own closet and holding a forged copy of the will, Lior becomes the prime suspect. As the investigation deepens, Lior realizes the killer is someone with access to the firm's confidential case files, someone reconstructing a decades-old injustice Vivian was about to expose. The killer is Lior's mentor, senior partner Edmund Hale, who murdered Vivian to bury the forged will that would have disinherited him and restored her fortune to the family he cheated. In the climax, Lior baits Edmund with a fake second will; Edmund's confession, recorded in the presence of the detective who finally believes Lior, ends the case—and Lior, once the firm's invisible workhorse, claims both the truth and a new sense of belonging among Vivian's estranged heirs.
about_author: Mirabel Dunmore is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's last words before writing her own. She lives in a drafty coastal house and insists every mystery she writes begins with a document that lies.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Lior Galloway's POV. Lior arrives at gloomy Marsh House to read Vivian Marsh's will and is stunned to be named executor and witness in a document the firm has no record of drafting. The beat is quiet unease—the first crack in Lior's carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A body is discovered in the conservatory wearing Lior's missing gray coat and scarf, clutching a second, contradictory will. Police treat Lior as suspect, not counsel. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being seen for the first time, in the worst way.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Detective Okafor POV. Okafor, skeptical but fair, notes the staged scene is 'too neat.' Lior realizes the killer knows the firm's file conventions intimately. Beat: wary alliance begins; Lior stops denying and starts investigating.

chapters.title: The Firm's Quiet Rooms
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior returns to the office and finds the Marsh file altered—dates shifted, a memo missing. Senior partner Edmund Hale offers comforting support and a warning about 'complicating things.' Beat: dread beneath loyalty; the reader senses the mentor's shadow.

chapters.title: Vivian's Letters
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with a letter from Vivian in italics. Among the estate papers Lior finds letters hinting Vivian was investigating a betrayal from thirty years ago involving a stolen inheritance. Beat: the victim gains a voice; the mystery gains stakes.

chapters.title: The Marsh Heirs
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior meets the estranged heirs: bitter nephew Theo, fragile cousin Anne, and Anne's watchful daughter Priya, each with alibis that are slightly too ready. Beat: Lior, an outsider, begins to feel an odd belonging among the dispossessed.

chapters.title: A Question of Handwriting
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Forensics confirms the coat's buttons were swapped and the second will forged by someone with genuine drafting skill. Okafor quietly narrows the suspect pool to legal insiders. Beat: the professional world Lior trusted becomes the crime scene.

chapters.title: The Missing Year
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Digging into archives, Lior finds a gap in the firm's history: a partner, Ruth Marsh—Vivian's sister—pushed out decades ago, her clients absorbed by Hale. Beat: anger; Lior sees the pattern of erasure and recognizes their own invisible life in it.

chapters.title: What the Housekeeper Saw
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The housekeeper, Mrs. Vane, admits Vivian met a 'gentleman from the city' twice before her death and left an envelope with the solicitor 'she trusted.' Beat: hope curdling—the trusted solicitor was almost certainly Hale.

chapters.title: Threat in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Someone ransacks Lior's office; the original will is gone. A typed note quotes the file's internal code words—proof the killer reads the case better than the investigators. Beat: fear turns personal; Lior can no longer stay invisible or safe.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Pressure from above pushes Okafor to charge Lior; Okafor resists, sharing evidence off the record instead. Beat: trust tested and deepened; two lonely professionals choose each other's honesty.

chapters.title: Anne's Confession
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Anne breaks down, admitting Vivian summoned her to witness a will that night—but Anne fled when she saw a man's car. Her description matches Hale's. Beat: guilt and relief; the heirs' fractured loyalty mirrors Lior's own.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts Hale obliquely; Hale deflects with perfect warmth, then reveals he knows Lior searched the archives. Beat: the mask slips just enough; loyalty and truth become impossible to hold at once.

chapters.title: Priya's Photograph
chapters.summary: Lior and Priya POV. Priya produces a photo of the conservatory taken that night: the 'body' staged before the murder occurred—someone rehearsing the frame. Beat: the case inverts; the killer needed a body that fit the clothes, not the clothes that fit the body.

chapters.title: The Second Envelope
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following Mrs. Vane's clue, Lior locates the envelope Vivian left: a true will restoring the Marsh fortune to Ruth's line and naming Hale's fraud. Beat: triumph shadowed by danger—now Lior holds the thing worth killing for.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The original will 'surfaces' in Lior's apartment, planted with Lior's fingerprints. Okafor is ordered to arrest. Beat: the trap closes; Lior's invisibility becomes a noose.

chapters.title: The Bait
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, tense and clipped. From custody-adjacent hiding, Lior drafts a fake 'second true will' and leaks its location—Marsh House, midnight. Beat: the hunted becomes hunter; resolve hardens into strategy.

chapters.title: Conservatory, Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Okafor POV. Hale comes for the document; Okafor, finally convinced, records as Hale gloats over the 'will' and confesses the murder and the thirty-year theft. Beat: climax—the killer undone by his own certainty.

chapters.title: What Hale Buried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Hale, arrested, explains himself with chilling calm: he erased Ruth Marsh the way the firm erases everyone inconvenient. Beat: cold aftermath; Lior confronts how close loyalty came to complicity.

chapters.title: The True Reading
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior reads Vivian's real will to the heirs: Ruth's line restored, Theo and Anne provided for, Priya named to the family trust. Beat: grief and grace; a document finally tells the truth.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya asks Lior to stay on as the estate's counsel; Lior, who spent a lifetime being unseen, accepts a place at the table. Beat: warmth; inheritance redefined as connection, not money.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Lior files the final report, adds a note to the case file in their own hand—visible, permanent—and visits Vivian's grave to report the truth delivered. Beat: quiet closure; the invisible lawyer signs their name.
